message.content: {"caption":"A left-to-right timeline showing test-time strategies developing from basic link-finding to more comprehensive checks and reasoning.","description":"A diagram arranged along a gray, curving progression with several small circular nodes and colored markers. Beneath it, a horizontal line labeled “Test-time Learning Timeline” ends in a right-pointing arrow, indicating progression from left to right. The stages and their associated descriptions are: “Procedural/execution strategy,” paired with a hand-clicking icon and the text “…, actively look for and click on ‘Next Page,’ ‘Page X,’ or ‘Load More’ links.”; “Atomic self-reflection,” paired with a magnifying-glass icon and the text “… it’s crucial to first re-check the element’s current identifier …”; “Evolved adaptive check,” paired with a target-like icon and the text “Before scanning, always leverage any available search or filter functionalities, ensure completeness before reporting …”; and “Generalized complex/effective strategy,” paired with a compass-like icon and the text “Regularly cross-referencing the current view with the task requirements helps prevent errors … If the current data doesn’t align with expectations (e.g., contents are incorrect or irrelevant), reassess available options such as search filters, alternative sections …”. The phrases “first re-check,” “look for,” “click on,” “leverage,” “ensure,” “cross-referencing,” “prevent errors,” “doesn’t align with expectations,” and “reassess” are highlighted in blue. The icons illustrate the corresponding actions: clicking navigation links, inspecting an identifier, checking search or filter results, and navigating a broader strategy. The curving path and right-pointing timeline arrow connect the stages in order.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
